overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation in the Board's appointment of an Emergency Management Director and alternate without notice of the topic, and found no evidence of pre-meeting deliberation. It reminded the Board to respond to complaints within 14 business days.

allegations.summary: Board appointed an Emergency Management Director and alternate at its August 11, 2010 meeting without listing the appointments in the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: The chair of the Board did not reasonably anticipate the appointments because Selectman Cavanaugh did not communicate to the chair that he would be raising the appointments that night.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly discussed the EMD appointments among members before the August 11, 2010 meeting, outside a properly noticed session.
allegations.key_passage: Selectman Cavanaugh specifically stated during the Board's August 11, 2010 meeting that he never discussed EMD candidate preferences with the other Board members prior to that night's open meeting, and we have not been presented with any evidence to the contrary.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly did not publicly interview or discuss all EMD candidates at an open meeting before appointing them.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Board did not discuss the candidates that Selectman Cavanaugh put forth before voting to approve them, we find no evidence that deliberation occurred prior to the open meeting.

allegations.summary: Board took more than three months to respond to the complaint, though the Open Meeting Law requires a response within 14 business days.
allegations.key_passage: As a final matter, we note that the Board took more than three months to respond to Ms. O'Connor's complaint.
